title: Support the `$/` self-repository `uses:` syntax
body:
Closes #711.

A `uses:` value starting with `$/` resolves against the repository running the workflow at the exact commit running it, so it carries no `@ref` and needs no checkout. GitHub [added the form][changelog] on 2026-07-30, and it is accepted everywhere the workspace-relative `./` form is — workflow steps, composite action steps, nested composition, and reusable workflow calls.

actionlint 1.7.12 reports it as a malformed repository reference:

```
example.yml:8:15: specifying action "$/.github/actions/my-action" in invalid format because ref is missing. available formats are "{owner}/{repo}@{ref}" or "{owner}/{repo}/{path}@{ref}" [action]
```

## Approach

`canonLocalUsesSpec`, in the new `uses.go`, normalises `$/{path}` to `./{path}` and reports whether a spec is local at all. Every site that previously tested `strings.HasPrefix(spec, "./")` now goes through it.

Normalising rather than teaching each call site a second prefix is what the metadata caches need. They are keyed by spec, and `LocalReusableWorkflowCache.WriteWorkflowCallEvent` writes its keys in the `./` form, so a workflow reached as `$/x.yml` would never find metadata written ahead of it.

`isWorkflowCallUsesRepoFormat` needed the prefix as well. It rejects a leading `.` so a local call is never mistaken for a repository one; without the same guard, `$/path/to/x.yml@ref` parsed as owner `$`, repo `path` and was accepted as a valid repository reference rather than reported.

The error message listing accepted reusable-workflow formats now names the third form, and `docs/checks.md` describes it alongside the other action types.

A step written `$/action@v1` is still accepted silently, because no directory named `action@v1` exists and actionlint deliberately does not complain about missing local action directories (#25, #40). That matches the existing behaviour of `./action@v1`, so I left it alone.

## Tests

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `uses_test.go` | `canonLocalUsesSpec` against both forms and the near-misses `$action`, `$`, `../action`; plus that both spellings of a path canonicalise identically, which is the property the caches depend on |
| `rule_workflow_call_test.go` | `$/path/to/x.yml` accepted; `$/path/to/x.yml@ref`, `$/` and `$` rejected |
| `testdata/projects/self_repository_uses/` | A project using `$/action` for a local action and `$/workflows/reusable.yaml` for a reusable workflow call |

The project fixture misspells the action's input in a second step, so its expected output asserts a missing-required-input and an undefined-input error. That proves the metadata behind `$/` is resolved rather than silently skipped, which an empty expected output could not distinguish.

`make test` and `make lint` pass — `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `scripts/check-checks`. Two failures on my machine are unrelated and reproduce on a clean checkout of `main`: `TestDetectErrorBadRequest` in `scripts/generate-popular-actions`, and `check-checks` on the pyflakes section when `pyflakes` is absent from `PATH`.

[changelog]: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-reference-same-repository-actions-with-self-repository-syntax/
